exodus.12.p1.b1.text: “This month is the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of your year.

exodus.12.p1.b2.text: on the tenth day of this month each man must select a lamb for his family, one per household.

exodus.12.p1.b3.text: If the household is too small for a whole lamb, they are to share with the nearest neighbor…

exodus.12.p1.b4.text: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male…

exodus.12.p2.b5.text: You must keep it until the fourteenth day of the month…

exodus.12.p2.b6.text: …the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel will slaughter the animals at twilight.

exodus.12.p2.b7.text: They are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs.

exodus.12.p2.b8.text: They are to eat the meat that night, roasted over the fire, along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

exodus.12.p3.b9.text: This is how you are to eat it: You must be fully dressed for travel, with your sandals on your feet and your staff in your hand. You are to eat in haste; it is the LORD’s Passover.

exodus.12.p3.b10.text: The blood on the houses where you are staying will distinguish them;

exodus.12.p3.b11.text: when I see the blood, I will pass over you.

exodus.12.p4.b12.text: And this day will be a memorial for you, and you are to celebrate it as a feast to the LORD, as a permanent statute for the generations to come.

exodus.12.p4.b13.text: For seven days you must eat unleavened bread.

exodus.12.p4.b14.text: On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly, and another on the seventh day.

exodus.12.p4.b15.text: …for on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt.

exodus.12.p5.b16.text: Go at once and select for yourselves a lamb for each family, and slaughter the Passover lamb.

exodus.12.p5.b17.text: None of you shall go out the door of his house until morning.

exodus.12.p5.b18.text: When your children ask you, ‘What does this service mean to you?’

exodus.12.p5.b19.text: It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites… and spared our homes.

exodus.12.p5.b20.text: Then the people bowed down and worshiped. And the Israelites went and did just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.

exodus.12.p6.b22.text: there was loud wailing in Egypt; for there was no house without someone dead.

exodus.12.p6.b23.text: During the night Pharaoh got up—he and all his officials and all the Egyptians—

exodus.12.p7.b24.text: Get up, leave my people, both you and the Israelites! Go, worship the LORD as you have requested.

exodus.12.p7.b25.text: Take your flocks and herds as well, just as you have said, and depart!

exodus.12.p8.b27.text: we are all going to die!

exodus.12.p8.b28.text: So the people took their dough before it was leavened, carrying it on their shoulders in kneading bowls wrapped in clothing.

exodus.12.p8.b29.text: And the LORD gave the people such favor in the sight of the Egyptians that they granted their request.

exodus.12.p9.b30.text: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children.

exodus.12.p9.b31.text: And a mixed multitude also went up with them, along with great droves of livestock, both flocks and herds.

exodus.12.p9.b32.text: the people baked what they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened loaves. For when they had been driven out of Egypt, they could not delay…

exodus.12.p10.b33.text: Now the duration of the Israelites’ stay in Egypt was 430 years.

exodus.12.p10.b34.text: At the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the LORD’s divisions went out of the land of Egypt.

exodus.12.p10.b35.text: Because the LORD kept a vigil that night… this same night is to be a vigil to the LORD, to be observed by all the Israelites for the generations to come.

exodus.12.p11.b36.text: This is the statute of the Passover: No foreigner is to eat of it.

exodus.12.p11.b37.text: you may not break any of the bones.

exodus.12.p11.b38.text: The same law shall apply to both the native and the foreigner who resides among you.”

exodus.12.p11.b39.text: Then all the Israelites did this—they did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron. And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions.
